g.text: STAGE 3 · ANALYSE — against the in-memory bundle, which still has source

g.title: e_cli
g.text: own disk — memory bounded to one bundle

g.title: scope
g.text: declared submission type — one per BATCH
The assignment's persisted default, or a per-request
override on ANY of the three upload routes.
An archive is REPO-SHAPED iff a non-junk entry sits under
a .provenance/ directory — decided from entry NAMES alone,
which a flat sealed bundle can never satisfy, so its staged
bytes (and therefore its dedup key) are unchanged

g.title: pfail
g.text: recorded on the job, not fatal
to the rest of the export

g.title: fanout
g.text: fan out — one job per scope × submitter
a scope is SEALED by either shape —
manifest a git submission's only seal

g.title: skiplist
g.text: submission_type_mismatch. A skipped scope has NO
ingest_files row — that is what being skipped means —
so the job summary, which counts rows, cannot report it.
Nullable with NO default: null = resolution unfinished,
[] = finished and skipped nothing. Collapsing those two
is how a heterogeneous batch read as clean.
Per SUBMISSION, never per batch: staging is
incremental with no transaction spanning it,
so aborting would strand a half-ingested one

g.title: dd
g.text: The DECLARED GROUP is asked FIRST —

g.title: ddskip
g.text: re-sending an unchanged bundle is cheap
— this is what lets provgate treat its

g.title: ddrefresh
g.text: only if the existing submission has no stored
submitted shas, and only once the upload is PROVEN the
same artifact: provenance entries byte-identical to the
stored blob's (never the zip bytes). Then restore the
shas, re-run validation + heuristics + score, write
an audit row and settle duplicate — one transaction

g.title: unm
g.text: surfaced in its own triage view —

g.title: val
g.text: check 2 walks the trust chain against the
configured ROOT public key — unset ⇒ skipped
and records their sha256s, so a later
re-run on the stripped blob agrees

g.title: lock
g.text: (semester_id, blob_sha256), then, for a grouped file only,
order, so two writers can never hold them crosswise and
deadlock; a file with no group key takes exactly one.
Two co-submitters carry byte-identical bundles, so both
cleared dedup before either committed and both created a
submission. Serial execution looked perfect; only

g.title: upa
g.text: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id,
falling back to SELECT — avoids a write

g.title: ver
g.text: raw FOR UPDATE over the cohort's rows so two
workers cannot claim the same index

g.title: mv
g.text: staging key → final key, inside the

g.title: fail
g.text: blob orphan left for the retention

g.title: contrib
g.text: establishBundleContributors MUTATES the bundle and several
heuristics read that stamp, so stamping earlier would change
which flags an ingest produces. Roster side and bundle side
reconcile onto ONE row per person; unattributed and
RE-CHECK each key inside its own lock —
a hit here is handled exactly as a
phase-2 hit: attach, do not create

g.title: done
g.text: a retry of this whole pipeline produces
byte-identical flags and stats — tests assert it
